comment_queue.text: @carmenuyamane It's Ebimaru Ramen in Nishi-Kanda, about a 4-min walk from Jimbocho Station (exit A4) or Suidobashi Station (east exit). They can be closed on Mondays, so check before you go 🦞

@lanarocha You'll eat well! Easy wins when kids get hungry: konbini (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) are on almost every corner with onigiri and sandwiches, department-store food floors (depachika) sell ready meals, and family restaurants like Gusto or Jonathan's have kids' menus. One heads-up: some tiny counter shops don't allow small kids, so keep a backup nearby 🐕
Lovely shots! If you're still in Tokyo: the main hall closes at 5pm, but the grounds stay open and the temple is lit up after sunset (until around 11pm), so it's much quieter at night 🏮
Your Akihabara day looks so fun! If you're there on a Sunday: Chuo-dori becomes a car-free pedestrian zone from 1-5pm (Oct-Mar, cancelled in bad weather) 🐕

comment_log.text: Love the Fujifilm tones! If you're back in Asakusa for lunch, Namiki Yabusoba (since 1913) is 2 min from the station, just note it's closed Thursdays.
comment_log.basis: shops.json Namiki Yabusoba: 2 min walk, closed Thursday; friend comment shows trip ongoing

comment_log.text: Great pond for reading! When you get hungry, Izuei Honten faces Shinobazu Pond and serves unaju (eel over rice) from ¥3,630, open 11:00-21:00 with an English menu.
comment_log.basis: shops.json Izuei Honten; post at Shinobazu Pond "read until I get hungry"

comment_log.text: Ueno in autumn looks lovely! If you're back in the park, Ueno Seiyoken inside it does hayashi rice and beef stew for lunch (closed Mondays).
comment_log.basis: shops.json Ueno Seiyoken; solo travel day 17 in Ueno

comment_log.text: Akihabara and Harajuku in one day! If you're back in Akihabara, Tsujita is 1 min from Suehirocho Station: rich tsukemen from ¥1,110, open every day (until 22:00 on weekdays).
comment_log.basis: shops.json Tsujita; first version said "open daily until 22:00" (weekends 21:30) → deleted and reposted

comment_log.text: Enjoy day 2! If you're near Ueno one evening, Daitoryo under the Ameyoko tracks serves skewers and stew until 23:30. Cash only, no booking needed.
Card hunting fuel: Shinpuku Saikan is 5 min from Akihabara Station, dark soy-sauce chuka soba from ¥880. Lunch 11:00-15:00, dinner from 17:30.
Lovely autumn walk! For a sweet stop after the park, Anmitsu Mihashi is 3 min from JR Ueno: cream anmitsu ¥760, open from 10:30.
Beautiful morning light! When lunch comes, Tonkatsu Yamabe is 1 min from Ueno-Hirokoji: a pork loin cutlet set for about ¥1,000, open from 11:00.
The egg sando is a must! For more snacks near Ueno, Niku no Oyama sells menchi-katsu from ¥150 at its standing counter, 2 min from Ueno Station.
Sounds like a perfect Day Three! If you head back to Akihabara, Shinpuku Saikan is 5 min from the station: Kyoto-style chuka soba from ¥880, open until 23:00 (it closes early if it sells out).
Congratulations on the honeymoon! If you're back in Ueno Park, Innsyoutei serves lunch inside the park from 11:00, and the basket lunch sets can be booked (from ¥2,950 on weekdays).
Fun start to day 3! For another early breakfast near Akihabara, Shin-Tagoto opens at 6:30 every day: standing soba and curry, 2 min from the station.
Beautiful colours in Ueno Park! If you pass by again in the morning, Coffee Ojo is a Showa-era coffee house 4 min from Ueno Station, open daily from 8:00 (cash or PayPay).
That otoshi surprise catches so many people! If you want an izakaya with no seat or otoshi charge, Yakiton Torahachi is 1 min from JR Akihabara Station and opens at 16:00 every day (pork skewers).
Glühwein in Ueno Park at night sounds perfect! For dinner right inside the park, Innsyoutei serves until 22:00 Mon–Sat (last order 21:30), about 10 min from Ueno Station.
Lovely family day in Ueno! For a sweet break near the park, Anmitsu Mihashi is 3 min from JR Ueno Station, open 10:30–21:00 on weekdays (to 19:30 on weekends).
Laundry break in Akihabara! When you get hungry, Shinpuku Saikan is 5 min from the station: dark soy-sauce ramen, 11:00–15:00 and 17:30–23:00.
Early Christmas in Ueno looks so fun! For a cheap snack nearby, Niku no Oyama (2 min from Ueno Station) sells menchi-katsu from ¥150, open until 22:00 on Sundays.
Lovely postcards from Ueno! If you explore again around lunch, Tonkatsu Yamabe is 1 min from Ueno-Hirokoji Station: pork loin cutlet sets, open daily 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–21:00.
Senso-ji looks lovely! For a warm sweet nearby, Umezono (2 min walk) serves awa zenzai, millet mochi with red bean paste, from ¥703. Weekends and holidays 10:00–18:00.
Great shot of the tracks! If you're back in Akihabara and hungry, Shin-Tagoto (2 min from the station) serves soba and steak curry, open daily 6:30–23:00.
Day 4 looks lovely! If you want lunch nearby, Izuei Honten (3 min from Ueno-Hirokoji Station) serves unaju, eel over rice, from ¥3,630. Open 11:00–21:00.
Senso-ji really is something! For a snack nearby, Asakusa Kokonoe (4 min from Asakusa Station) sells fried red-bean manju from ¥160, open daily 10:00–19:00.
Beautiful colours! If you want to warm up in Ueno, Coffee Dokoro Bonaru (3 min from Ueno-Hirokoji Station) is a smoke-free coffee house, open from 11:00. Cash only.
Day 8 already! If you're near Ueno again, Kurofunetei (2 min from Keisei Ueno) serves hayashi rice and omurice, with no service or table charge.
Day 8 in Ueno looks great! For a classic lunch nearby, Ponta Honke (1 min from Ueno-Hirokoji) serves katsuretsu, pork loin cutlet, from ¥4,070. Lunch 11:00–14:00, closed Mondays.
Love Ueno! For a retro coffee break nearby, Galan (2 min from JR Ueno) is an old-style kissaten, open daily 9:00–22:30. Cash only, and smoking is allowed inside.
Looks festive! If you want a late bite after the lights, Motsuyaki Daitoryo (2 min from JR Ueno) does grilled skewers from 2 for ¥180, open daily until 23:30.
